FBI CDE count / FBI CDE agency population * 1000

caveats: NYPD counts are complaints by report year under NY Penal Law categories (felony assault, grand + petit larceny), close to but not the same as FBI UCR definitions used elsewhere.
Rates use residents only; precincts with many workers or visitors look worse per resident.

categories.grand_larceny_motor_vehicle: ofns_desc 'GRAND LARCENY OF MOTOR VEHICLE' (ky_cd 110): pd_desc 'LARCENY,GRAND OF AUTO' (441), 'LARCENY, GRAND OF AUTO - ATTEM' (442), 'LARCENY, GRAND OF MOPED' (450), 'LARCENY,GRAND OF MOTORCYCLE' (451), 'LARCENY,GRAND OF TRUCK' (455)

crime_near.evening_share_method: share of last-24-month complaints with a recorded start time (cmplnt_fr_tm) whose start hour is 19 to 23. For thefts found later, the start time is the beginning of the window in which it could have happened.

provenance.source: NYPD Complaint Data Historic (qgea-i56i) and Current Year To Date (5uac-w243), NYC Open Data
provenance.method: count of complaints whose published latitude/longitude is within 250 m (planar distance) of the point

caveats: NYPD publishes the midpoint of the street segment or the nearest intersection, not the exact address, so a count at a small radius is approximate.
Complaints with no coordinates are left out: 2023: 0 of 107732, 2024: 1 of 100500, 2025: 0 of 98053, 2026: 1 of 66749 rows in the slice.
Counts are not divided by population: busy commercial streets and transit hubs collect more complaints.

vs_baseline.method: Regular 300 m grid over the NYPD precinct polygons; a grid point counts as residential when 2020 Census blocks with their internal point within 250 m hold at least 500 residents; the incidents_near counts (radius 250 m) are computed at every such point and summarised by median, 80th and 90th percentile.

cooking_only.method: National Grid NY (KEDNY: Brooklyn, Queens, Staten Island), SC 1A Residential Non-Heating Service: $23.50/month covers the first 3 therms (or Ccf) or less; gas supply for those therms, surcharges and taxes are extra (a few dollars) (effective 2026-04-01); assumed cooking use 1.6 therms/month (RECS 2020 microdata, Northeast apartments in 5+ unit buildings with gas cooking, n=108). Taxes not included.

cooking_plus_heat.method: cooking-only figure ($24) + NY average residential gas price $1.704/therm (EIA 2025 annual, $17.58/Mcf at 1032 Btu per cubic foot) x 11.7 therms/month of space heating (annual use / 12; RECS 2020 microdata, Northeast apartments in 5+ unit buildings heated with gas, n=124). An annual average: winter bills are several times higher and summer bills lower. Water heating is not included.
